summary: This corporate documentary segment from NPCIL highlights the refurbishment and life extension (En-Masse Coolant Channel Replacement - EMCCR and En-Masse Feeder Replacement - EMFR) of Rajasthan Atomic Power Station Unit 3 (RAPS-3) at Rawatbhata, Rajasthan. It features plant exteriors by the Rana Pratap Sagar lake, footage of OSART inspection, reactor core maintenance, automated retubing tools, fuel loading, control room operations, and statements by NPCIL leadership.

spans.speech: Rajasthan Atomic Power Station Unit 3 of Rawatbhata Rajasthan site, also known as RAPS 3, began its operations on June 1st, 2000, and has been a cornerstone of India's nuclear energy sector, driving progress and sustainability.

spans.shows: Garden pathways around the administration complex, cooling towers, and a monument commemorating 777 days of continuous operation.

spans.speech: RAPS 3 has been a trailblazer in many ways, from setting a record 777 days of continuous operation to running for more than a year on three separate occasions, this unit exemplifies operational excellence.

spans.speech: In 2012, RAPS 3 made history by hosting India's first ever OSART mission, conducted by the International Atomic Energy Agency. The mission, which reviewed the operational safety of RAPS 3 and 4, was a grand success, bringing global recognition to India's nuclear capabilities.
